# Objectives

BLM assumptions evaluated (two paired scenarios)

-   **Carbonate charge balance**

    -   Baseline: Closed system, measured DIC as input

    -   Perturbed: Open system, no DIC input, alkalinity estimated by charge balance (assuming in equilibrium with atmospheric partial pressure)

-   **Humic acid fraction of DOC**

    -   Baseline: HA = 10% (suggested by the BLM manual)

    -   Perturbed: HA = 80%

# 1. Setup

We will merge BLM output variables from the baseline conditions (closed system + HA 10%) and the perturbed scenarios (open system + HA 10% and closed system + HA 80%) which are currently organized into separate tabs within the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet.

First, we'll load all the necessary packages

```{r}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(e1071)
```

Next, we'll set the working directory and import each dataset as it's own object


# 2. Data organization

Now we'll read each file and create the following scenarios as their own objects

-   ha_10_cs

-   ha_10_os

-   ha_80_cs

```{r}
read_scenario <- function(path, sheet, scenario_label) {
  read_excel(path, sheet = sheet) %>%
    mutate(Scenario = scenario_label) %>%
    relocate(Scenario, .before = 1)
}

ha_10_cs <- read_scenario(file_master3, "HA 10% Closed System", "HA 10% Closed System")
ha_10_os <- read_scenario(file_master2, "HA 10% Open System",   "HA 10% Open System")
ha_80_cs <- read_scenario(file_master2, "HA 80% Closed System", "HA 80% Closed System")
```

Now we'll add typology to each scenario (ha_10_cs already has it)

```{r}
typology_lookup <- ha_10_cs %>%
  select(Sample_ID, Typology) %>%
  distinct()

ha_10_os <- ha_10_os %>% left_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID")
ha_80_cs <- ha_80_cs %>% left_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID")

# quick sanity check (should be character(0))
setdiff(ha_10_os$Sample_ID, ha_10_cs$Sample_ID)
setdiff(ha_80_cs$Sample_ID, ha_10_cs$Sample_ID)
```

Stack each scenario to create one long dataset (dat_long)

```{r}
dat_long <- bind_rows(ha_10_cs, ha_10_os, ha_80_cs)
head(dat_long)
```

# 4. Sensitivity calculations

Using one function, we'll create a paired dataset and calculate the delta, percent change, and log response ratio (LRR) for each variable

## I. Helper functions

### a. Create wide dataset

```{r}
make_pair_wide <- function(dat, scenarios, short_labels = c("Baseline", "Perturbed"), vars) {
  dat %>%
    filter(Scenario %in% scenarios) %>%
    mutate(Scenario_short = recode(Scenario,
                                  !!scenarios[1] := short_labels[1],
                                  !!scenarios[2] := short_labels[2])) %>%
    select(Sample_ID, Typology, Scenario_short, all_of(vars)) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Scenario_short,
      values_from = all_of(vars),
      names_sep = "_"
    )
}
```

### b. Calculate SA metrics

-   **Delta**: baseline − perturbed (matches your carbonate delta)

-   **Percent change**: (perturbed − baseline) / baseline \* 100 (matches your code)

-   **LRR**: log10(perturbed) − log10(baseline)

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

compute_sensitivity <- function(pair_wide, vars, baseline, perturbed) {

  # Helper to build the expected wide column names
  base_cols <- paste0(vars, "_", baseline)
  pert_cols <- paste0(vars, "_", perturbed)

  # Safety check: stop early with a clear message if something is missing
  missing_cols <- setdiff(c(base_cols, pert_cols), names(pair_wide))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("These columns are missing from pair_wide:\n", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }

  # -------------------------------------------------
  # 1) Delta: baseline - perturbed
  # -------------------------------------------------
  delta_df <- tibble(
    Sample_ID = pair_wide$Sample_ID,
    Typology  = pair_wide$Typology
  ) %>%
    bind_cols(
      as_tibble(setNames(
        lapply(vars, function(v) {
          pair_wide[[paste0(v, "_", baseline)]] - pair_wide[[paste0(v, "_", perturbed)]]
        }),
        paste0("delta_", vars)
      ))
    )

  # -------------------------------------------------
  # 2) Percent change: (perturbed - baseline) / baseline * 100
  # -------------------------------------------------
  pct_df <- tibble(
    Sample_ID = pair_wide$Sample_ID,
    Typology  = pair_wide$Typology
  ) %>%
    bind_cols(
      as_tibble(setNames(
        lapply(vars, function(v) {
          b <- pair_wide[[paste0(v, "_", baseline)]]
          p <- pair_wide[[paste0(v, "_", perturbed)]]

          ifelse(!is.na(b) & b != 0, (p - b) / b * 100, NA_real_)
        }),
        paste0("pct_", vars)
      ))
    )

  # -------------------------------------------------
  # 3) Log response ratio: log10(perturbed) - log10(baseline)
  # -------------------------------------------------
  lrr_df <- tibble(
    Sample_ID = pair_wide$Sample_ID,
    Typology  = pair_wide$Typology
  ) %>%
    bind_cols(
      as_tibble(setNames(
        lapply(vars, function(v) {
          b <- pair_wide[[paste0(v, "_", baseline)]]
          p <- pair_wide[[paste0(v, "_", perturbed)]]

          ifelse(!is.na(b) & !is.na(p) & b > 0 & p > 0, log10(p) - log10(b), NA_real_)
        }),
        paste0("dlog10_", vars)
      ))
    )

  # Return everything neatly
  list(pair_wide = pair_wide, delta = delta_df, pct = pct_df, lrr = lrr_df)
}

```

### c. Wilcoxon tests

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper 1: Run paired Wilcoxon tests for ONE comparison
# ------------------------------------------------------------
run_wilcox_paired <- function(dat_long, baseline_scn, perturbed_scn, log_vars) {

  # 1) Make a long table of log variables for the two scenarios
  long_dat <- dat_long %>%
    filter(Scenario %in% c(baseline_scn, perturbed_scn)) %>%
    select(Sample_ID, Scenario, all_of(log_vars)) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(log_vars),
      names_to = "Variable",
      values_to = "Log_Value"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Variable = str_remove(Variable, "^log_"),
      Metal = case_when(
        str_detect(Variable, "Zn") ~ "Zn",
        str_detect(Variable, "Cu") ~ "Cu",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Metal))

  # 2) Pivot wide so each Sample_ID has baseline and perturbed side-by-side
  wide_dat <- long_dat %>%
    select(Sample_ID, Scenario, Variable, Metal, Log_Value) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Scenario, values_from = Log_Value)

  # 3) Run paired Wilcoxon test per Variable
  wilcox_tbl <- wide_dat %>%
    group_by(Variable, Metal) %>%
    summarise(
      n_pairs = sum(!is.na(.data[[baseline_scn]]) & !is.na(.data[[perturbed_scn]])),
      p_value = wilcox.test(
        x = .data[[baseline_scn]],
        y = .data[[perturbed_scn]],
        paired = TRUE,
        exact = FALSE
      )$p.value,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      sig_label = case_when(
        p_value <= 0.001 ~ "***",
        p_value <= 0.01  ~ "**",
        p_value <= 0.05  ~ "*",
        TRUE ~ ""
      )
    )

  list(long_dat = long_dat, wilcox_tbl = wilcox_tbl)
}
```

## III. Carbonate assumption SA

### a. Paired dataset

```{r}
dic_pair <- make_pair_wide(
  dat = dat_long,
  scenarios = c("HA 10% Closed System", "HA 10% Open System"),
  short_labels = c("Closed", "Open"),
  vars = response_vars
)

dic_sa <- dic_pair

dic_results <- compute_sensitivity(
  pair_wide = dic_sa,
  vars = response_vars,
  baseline = "Closed",
  perturbed = "Open"
)

dic_delta  <- dic_results$delta
dic_pct    <- dic_results$pct
dic_dlog10 <- dic_results$lrr
```

### b. Summary statistics

```{r}
summarise_metric <- function(metric_df, prefix, vars) {
  metric_df %>%
    select(starts_with(prefix)) %>%
    setNames(vars) %>%                     # drop prefix in column names
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>%
    group_by(Variable) %>%
    summarise(
      Mean   = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
      Median = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q1     = quantile(Value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q3     = quantile(Value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      IQR    = IQR(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Metal = case_when(
        str_detect(Variable, "Zn") ~ "Zn",
        str_detect(Variable, "Cu") ~ "Cu",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Metal)) %>%
    group_by(Metal) %>%
    arrange(Median, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      Variable = factor(Variable, levels = Variable),
      Rank = row_number()
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Tables to help plot
plot_pct_dic <- summarise_metric(dic_pct, prefix = "pct_", vars = response_vars)
plot_lrr_dic <- summarise_metric(dic_dlog10, prefix = "dlog10_", vars = response_vars)
```

Save summary statistics

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

```

### c. Plots (percent change + LRR)

Faceted

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

plot_summary_bars <- function(df, xlab, title, subtitle, fill_name) {
  ggplot(df, aes(y = Variable)) +
    geom_col(aes(x = Median, fill = Median)) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Q1, xmax = Q3), height = 0.25) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
    facet_wrap(~ Metal, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "red3", mid = "grey95", high = "steelblue4",
      midpoint = 0,
      name = fill_name
    ) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL, title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_bw() +
    guides(fill = "none")
}

# Percent change plot
p_pct_dic <- plot_summary_bars(
  plot_pct_dic,
  xlab = "Percent Change (Open vs Closed)",
  title = "Sensitivity of BLM outputs to carbonate system assumption",
  subtitle = "Bars = median; error bars = IQR",
  fill_name = "% Change"
)

# LRR plot
p_lrr_dic <- plot_summary_bars(
  plot_lrr_dic,
  xlab = "Log Response Ratio (Open vs Closed)",
  title = "Sensitivity of BLM outputs to carbonate system assumption",
  subtitle = "Bars = median; error bars = IQR",
  fill_name = "Median LRR"
)

p_pct_dic
p_lrr_dic
```

### d. Wilcoxon paired tests

```{r}
baseline_scn <- "HA 10% Closed System"
dic_pert_scn <- "HA 10% Open System"

dic_wilcox <- run_wilcox_paired(
  dat_long      = dat_long,
  baseline_scn  = baseline_scn,
  perturbed_scn = dic_pert_scn,
  log_vars      = log_response_vars
)

# Add p-values + sig labels back onto the plotting data
dic_plot_dat_sig <- dic_wilcox$long_dat %>%
  left_join(dic_wilcox$wilcox_tbl %>% select(Variable, p_value, n_pairs, sig_label),
            by = "Variable")

# View
View(dic_plot_dat_sig)
```

```{r}
ha_pert_scn <- "HA 80% Closed System"

ha_wilcox <- run_wilcox_paired(
  dat_long      = dat_long,
  baseline_scn  = baseline_scn,
  perturbed_scn = ha_pert_scn,
  log_vars      = log_response_vars
)

# Add p-values + sig labels back onto plotting data
ha_plot_dat_sig <- ha_wilcox$long_dat %>%
  left_join(ha_wilcox$wilcox_tbl %>% select(Variable, p_value, n_pairs, sig_label),
            by = "Variable")

# View
View(ha_plot_dat_sig)
```

Save table

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

  addWorksheet(wb, "Wilcoxon tests")

# Save the workbook (overwrite) 
saveWorkbook(wb, "Sensitivity_analysis_dic_assumptions.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```
